authority_basis.summary: Operator directed the resident agent through the surya research program attack order; task #5 (R3 gap map) is claimed and this admission is its evidence record.

operations.method: Four parallel web research sweeps (ELO throughput/scale; substrate reuse cycles/reprep economics; IMM mechanical reliability; player claims MicroLink/Rocket Lab/AZUR/NREL/Fraunhofer ISE) via WebSearch/FetchURL subagents; sources typed peer-reviewed / government-lab / company-claim / secondary.
operations.result: Substrate liberation is physically demonstrated at cell level but economically undemonstrated: binding constraint is per-cycle reconditioning cost and throughput, not reuse count; demonstrated reuse is <=4 cycles (GaAs) and 1 (Ge); no published production throughput/yield, no space qualification of substrate-free product.

R3 gap map: substrate liberation via ELO/IMM is physically demonstrated at cell level (13 um epi stacks, ~31% AM0, >3000 W/kg cell-level, film-laminated flight heritage) but economically undemonstrated - the binding constraints are per-cycle substrate reconditioning cost and process throughput, not reuse cycle count; no public evidence shows reuse beyond ~4 cycles (GaAs) or 1 cycle (Ge), production-scale throughput or yield, or space qualification of substrate-free product.

ELO throughput: classic HF ELO is diffusion-limited to 0.1-0.3 mm/h lateral undercut; best published rates reach 15-30 mm/h with stressor/mechanical enhancement, still implying hours per 6-inch wafer per station; constellation-relevant volume (order 1,550 six-inch lift-offs/day for 10,000 m2/yr) is >100x beyond any demonstrated facility; no per-wafer yield figures are published anywhere.

Reuse cycles: the ~10-cycles threshold circulating in cost literature is an assumption, not an experimental result - demonstrated reuse is 4 cycles (GaAs 1997, materials metrics only), 'multiple' (MicroLink IMM 2013, count not public), and 1 for Ge (porous-Ge 2023; spalled-Ge 2022); per NREL TEA the per-cycle reconditioning cost (CMP est. 10-40 um/cycle, $9-34/cell) binds before cycle count; Ge reuse after classic AlAs-sacrificial ELO is undemonstrated.

Mechanical integration: substrate-free IMM/ELO cells are held by metal carrier stacks (Au/Cu) or polymer/silicone laminates; cell-level >3000 W/kg and JAXA Space Solar Sheet ~600 W/kg demonstrated; but no published AIAA S-111/ECSS-E-ST-20-08C qualification of substrate-free product, no cyclic-flexure dataset, no on-orbit degradation data for substrate-free multijunction III-V; MicroLink flight heritage is stratospheric (HAPS), and Cu carriers fail catastrophically (>60% loss) under 200 C accelerated ageing vs ~10% for Au.

Players: only MicroLink commercially deploys ELO (HAPS scale; certified 37.75% AM1.5G research cell; 29% AM0 production datasheet; no published throughput/yield/cost; space qualification only started ~2021 per company); Rocket Lab/SolAero production IMM removes but does not reuse substrates; AZUR addresses the Ge chokepoint via backgrinding-waste recycling, not lift-off; Fraunhofer ISE runs a reusable-template program (EpiWafer) without published cell data; ESA-ELLA (Umicore) demonstrates 200 mm engineered Ge substrates at lab scale with 2x reuse.

evidence.paraphrase: IMM4J thin-film cell: 13 um epi stack, 140 g/m2, >3000 W/kg cell level, 30.9% AM0 BOL; handling cracks and shunts documented in unsupported films; metal layer stack serves as mechanical carrier.

JAXA Space Solar Sheet: IMM-3J on 10-20 um film, <0.2 mm total, ~600 W/kg sheet level, >150 W/kg paddle; internal qual tests passed within +/-2.5% with no crack propagation (test matrix table not extractable).
Accelerated ageing at 200 C: thin-film cells on Au carrier lose ~10% after 37 days; on Cu carrier >60% (Cu diffusion, film curling); ELO peel-bend itself introduced no device damage.
Diffusion-reaction model: maximum lateral etch rate bounded by H2 out-diffusion through the narrowing etched gap; basis for the 0.1-0.3 mm/h classic ELO ceiling.
20 mm/h lateral etch with internal sacrificial stressor layers plus acetone-HF, described as fastest reported; implies ~3.75 h per 6-inch wafer (derived).
NREL bottom-up TEA of ELO, spalling, porous-Ge: cost reduction from reuse is limited not by achievable cycle count but by per-cycle substrate re-preparation cost.
III-V cell MSP $70-170+/WDC at 50-200 kW/yr; Ge substrate single largest cost; whether reuse beyond 5-10 cycles lowers cost appreciably depends on CMP/reclaim costs.
GaAs substrate reused four times after ELO with wet-chemical cleaning; no decrease in ELO film minority-carrier lifetime or mobility.
MicroLink demonstrates multiple substrate reuses for IMM cells on 4-inch GaAs; exact cycle count not stated in accessible text (paywalled).
PEELER porous-Ge: 100 mm Ge wafer, one reuse demonstrated with wet-etch reconditioning (RMS 20.1 to 1.3 nm), ~30 reuses projected; 0.27 g Ge per cycle vs 6.06 g per conventional 145 um wafer.
ELO is currently the only commercially deployed substrate reuse technology; CMP re-polish estimated $9-34 per cell; Ge/GaAs substrate >$30/W; 23.4% GaInAs cell on spalled Ge without polishing.
MicroLink 37.75% 3J ELO cell NREL-certified under AM1.5G on 6-inch GaAs production platform; >3000 W/kg AM0 claimed but not certified; production datasheet 29% AM0, <350 g/m2.

IMM-beta ~33.3% avg BOL entering qualification, 87% power remaining after 1 MeV electrons 1e15 e/cm2; product pages list IMM-beta as space-qualified; no ELO or wafer-reuse claim from Rocket Lab/SolAero.
Umicore ELLA: 190 mm detachable Ge foil on 200 mm wafer via GeON/porous Ge, wafer reused 2x, 3J cells on 7 um Ge foil performing similar to controls; lab-scale feasibility.
First flight demonstration of film-laminated thin-film InGaP/GaAs 2J cells in LEO (JAXA SDS, 2009); no IMM/ELO multijunction on-orbit dataset exists.
Current III-V cell cost ~$150/W; no public $/W price for any ELO-based product.

operations.reason: Four independent sweeps converge: substrate-liberation physics is demonstrated at cell level and in HAPS/early LEO flight, but every economic leg of R3 (cycle count, reprep cost, throughput, space qualification of substrate-free product) rests on assumptions or company claims rather than published demonstration. Gaps enumerated: ELO yield, per-wafer lift-off time in production, demonstrated Ge reuse after classic ELO, space-qual and flexure datasets for thin-film III-V, ELO product $/W.
